entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Postumus Aebutius Helva Cornicen was a Roman consul in 442 BC and magister equitum in 435, playing a key role in the governance of Rome during the late Republic.






This event was caused by the power struggle between the Roman Senate and the growing influence of the equites, a group of wealthy and powerful Roman citizens who sought to limit the power of the Senate.






As a result, Postumus Aebutius Helva Cornicen's leadership helped to stabilize the Roman Republic and maintain the balance of power between the Senate and the equites.







The legacy of Postumus Aebutius Helva Cornicen can be seen in the continued development of the Roman Republic's governance structure, which would eventually give rise to the Principate under Augustus.






In conclusion, the Roman historian Tacitus wrote, 'The virtues of a good man are not to be measured by his achievements, but by the virtues he possesses.'
